key_evidence_spans: She had been diagnosed with a tenosynovial giant cell tumor by MRI at a local hospital
The median nerve was mildly compressed and deformed, and degenerative changes were noted in some carpal bones
Noncontrast MRI of the right hand demonstrated patchy abnormal signal around the deep flexor tendons and carpal canal
Ultrasonography showed rough, thickened bone surfaces and decreased echogenicity at the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints and along multiple flexor tendons
Laboratory studies showed normal leukocyte count, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate; rheumatoid factor was negative
Post-contrast images demonstrated homogeneous enhancement of the tendons and synovial membrane, supporting synovial hyperplasia
Diffusion-weighted imaging and ADC maps suggested restricted diffusion
